turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Deshmukh, before you go in, I have your readings. Blood pressure is 138 over 86, pulse 78, temperature 36.8, oxygen saturation 98 percent. Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergy, sister. I hardly take tablets.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Good. Please go through, doctor is at his desk. He may be a little caught up on the computer.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ah, come, come. Sorry, um, this screen has frozen again. Give me one moment. Right, what is the problem today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing much, doctor. Back is paining a little, that is all. She dragged me here.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is not nothing. Every evening he is holding the low back and sitting crooked.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that once more? A notification popped up. The back, yes?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Low back, doctor. Only mild. I am managing.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): A few weeks. Since we shifted house and I lifted all those boxes. It will go by itself.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The move was six weeks ago. The pain started that week, when the sofa was carried up.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Arre, two or three weeks of actual pain. Before that I was just tired from the shifting. I don't keep dates, what is the use.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wait, I lost you. Was it two weeks, or, well, actually from the time of the move? Tell me again slowly.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): From the move. About six weeks. I remember because the packing boxes were still in the hall.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, fine, since the move then. Call it six weeks if you want. Still not a big thing.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where does it sit, and does the pain travel down the leg?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Middle of the low back, a bit to the right side. It does not travel. It stays in the back only.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): What brings it on, and what eases it?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Right side of the low back. Lifting sacks and bending make it worse, evenings especially, and lying flat eases it. It is three or four out of ten, nothing terrible. Mornings I am stiff for about ten minutes and then I go to work.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And those sacks are fifty kilos. Rice bags. He should not be doing that.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): It is the job only. I am not some patient who cannot walk.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Three or four, you said? I was typing the last note. And the work is?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Manual loading, at the godown near the market. Yes, three or four. Hardly anything.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Coming here the traffic was terrible, and the whole way he had the cricket on.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): India were 140 for 2 when we locked the house. Kohli was batting so well. That cover drive yesterday, did you watch?
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was packing the tiffin, I didn't watch. Your brother said the pitch was slow and the bowlers had no help.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Slow pitch and he still found the gap. If it rains this evening they will cover the ground and the match is gone. Monsoon has come early, the balcony was dripping.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We should have taken the inner road. Jubilee Hills side was one long jam, horns nonstop.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hmm, what was that? I was stuck in the medication list. Were you saying something about the pain?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no, that was just the match and the traffic. Forget it. About the back I already told you, it is minor.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. I have to check a few danger things, one at a time. Any numbness or pins and needles in the legs or the feet?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Legs are completely fine.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Again, please, the cursor jumped. Any numbness?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No numbness, no tingling. Nothing in the legs.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bladder? Any difficulty passing urine, any leaking, any numb feeling in that area?

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of that. Passing urine is normal, no leaking. I do wake once in the night, but that is, um, a full mug of chai before bed. The match was on, so what to do, I made tea.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every night the same chai story. But truly, doctor, no leaking, I would have noticed.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): So no loss of control. Have you lost weight?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Lost weight? No chance. Appetite is the same as always. I am eating fine.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Even a low one, or chills?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no chills. I am not ill. It is only this work pain.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): What painkiller have you used?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin. I swallow one 500 milligram tablet when it is bad, usually at night. Not daily. Maybe twice in a week.
[SEG0044] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I have seen him take two tablets some nights.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): That was one time by mistake and I didn't like it. Normally it is one, 500 only. Don't make it sound like I am on drugs.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else you take regularly? Any old test I should know about?

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing regular. Last year at the company health check they did my sugar. They said it was borderline. No number, just borderline, repeat next year, and I never took a tablet for it.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline, and they didn't give you the figure. I won't, um, invent one. Let me look at the back. Please stand and bend forward slowly.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mild tenderness in the muscles on the right side of the low back. Forward bending is a little restricted. Straight leg raise is free on both sides, and when I check the feet I am not finding numbness.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): There, you see. Nothing. So I can do my shift tomorrow, yes?

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): From what you tell me and from this exam, this is most likely a simple mechanical back pain, a muscle strain from the lifting. No red flag features. Please stay off the fifty kilo sacks for at least a week. Keep walking around the house, and no bed rest.

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am prescribing naproxen 500 mg by mouth, twice a day after food, for five days, for this back pain. You may still swallow the Crocin when you need it, that combination is acceptable. If it has not settled in two weeks we might arrange a lower back X-ray. I am not ordering any scan today.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Book a review in two weeks with reception. Come earlier if the leg becomes weak, if numbness starts, if bladder control changes, or if you get a fever. Sorry, I have to finish this screen before the next person.
